submission_readiness.reasoning: A coherent and empirically promising local draft, but remaining claim calibration, comparative uncertainty and editorial work are advisable. Target venue/cycle/stage and submission-form obligations remain unconfirmed. Baseline adaptation settings also need documentation.

headline_verdict: The revised paper merits an internal overall score of 3/5 (borderline), up from 2/5. Replay membership, normalized ranking, global skill-balanced splits and frozen-retriever status are now explicit. The remaining material concerns are incomplete non-parametric baseline protocol reporting, comparison-level uncertainty and an unsupported backbone-ceiling inference. This is a manuscript assessment, not an official ARR rating or certification of historical experimental provenance.

review_form.summary: RouterBSI routes retrieved skills using natural-language applicability predicates and refines failed predicates through minimum empirical replay risk and a held-out validation gate relative to initialization. Six SRA-Bench task collections share a large skill corpus; the paper measures routing, retention, downstream success and component/backbone sensitivity. Weights remain fixed while predicates adapt.
strengths: Explicit, editable routing criteria with a coherent risk-minimization and validation procedure (§4).
Coverage across six task collections, three retrievers, strong frozen SkillRouter comparison, and separate routing/downstream measurements (§5–7).
Table 1 aggregates reproduce from saved per-dataset means; RouterBSI leads the reported overall routing metrics while dataset reversals and SkillDAG downstream advantage are acknowledged.
Appendix documents exact splits, prompts, settings, gate behavior and evaluator limitations, including class-imbalance and non-human-adjudication caveats.
Recent corrections resolve the principal manuscript-internal setup inconsistencies.
weaknesses: The paper does not specify the Skill-Pro and SkillDAG adaptation configurations sufficiently to reproduce or interpret the optimizer comparison. (ISSUE-006).
The main comparative advantage is supported by point estimates without paired uncertainty for the reported method comparisons. (ISSUE-007).
Three backbone endpoints do not establish an irreducible predicate-capacity ceiling. (ISSUE-009).
The main cost trade-off omits the single-run and recorded-token scope that is supplied in Appendix G.2. (ISSUE-008).
The dependency explanation is not isolated from differing skill budgets and baseline mechanisms. (ISSUE-010).
The main metric shorthand does not distinguish selected-set F1 from ranked-cutoff metrics, and the retention aggregation is defined only in the appendix. (ISSUE-011).
Persistent grammatical and notation defects reduce clarity of the core method and figure captions. (ISSUE-012).
Figure 4 has an ungrammatical headline caption and unnecessarily small labels for a full-width chart. (ISSUE-013).
questions: Can paired task-level predictions support confidence intervals for RouterBSI versus SkillRouter on routing and downstream outcomes?
What actual training-signal, adaptation-budget and checkpoint-selection settings were used for Skill-Pro and SkillDAG?
Will the backbone-ceiling statement be narrowed to the tested endpoints?
What exact model roles correspond to every model listed in §5.3?
Can historically bound initialization records settle the separate Figure 5 artifact question? The manuscript passages themselves agree.

soundness.justification: Core empirical-risk selection and cold-start gate are coherent; source/table checks support observed gains. Single-run competitor comparisons lack paired uncertainty and scaling interpretation overreaches. The Skill-Pro/SkillDAG adaptation configurations are insufficiently specified, limiting reproducibility without proving unfairness.

presentation.justification: Recent replay, normalization, split and training clarifications materially improve coherence. Persistent method grammar, ambiguous captions and small figure labels keep presentation mixed.

contribution.justification: A relevant NLP/agent-routing contribution combining editable skill predicates, bounded empirical replay selection and a held-out gate, evaluated across six datasets. Novelty is the particular routing representation and update design, not a new generic risk principle.

overall.justification: The revised manuscript is borderline, improved from substantial revision: several central contradictions are resolved and observed aggregate benefits are supported, but comparative precision and the backbone-ceiling interpretation remain material weaknesses. Baseline-protocol documentation also remains incomplete.

confidence.justification: Fresh snapshot/source review, independent audits, figure inspection, live official-policy checks and saved-table reaggregation. No new training, human validation, or historical artifact-binding verification.

issues.title: Baseline adaptation and resource matching are not sufficiently documented to isolate method advantage

location.quoted_text: SkillRouter likewise uses its released reranker checkpoint without fine-tuning on our task-training split.

supporting_evidence.quoted_text: Compared to the other non-parametric optimization baselines, RouterBSI has a mean 29.2\% and 26.7\% nDCG@10 score over SkillDAG and Skill-Pro, respectively.

issues.problem: The paper does not specify the Skill-Pro and SkillDAG adaptation configurations sufficiently to reproduce or interpret the optimizer comparison.
reasoning_chain: 1. Section 5 describes the frozen retrievers/SkillRouter and RouterBSI ten-iteration optimization clearly.

2. The same section names Skill-Pro and SkillDAG as non-parametric optimization baselines, but their adaptation settings, feedback use and checkpoint selection are not specified in the current source. Appendix D.4 details retrieval and task evaluation rather than those baseline protocols.

3. Baseline citations do not uniquely specify the adaptations to the shared skill pool and current split. This is a material reproducibility and interpretation gap, not proof of unfair implementation.
counterevidence: The frozen-checkpoint status is now explicit: there is no remaining ambiguity about whether SkillRouter or retrievers were fine-tuned.

The main text reports a shared top-50 pool, the SkillDAG expansion exception and its ranking rule; Appendix H.3 verifies identical ordered top-50 candidates for the matched two-dataset SkillRouter analysis.
RouterBSI initialization/final comparisons and the component ablation already provide useful within-method controls.
A same-data neural fine-tuning experiment is not mandatory if the claim is limited to black-box adaptation versus the reported deployed configurations.
issues.predicted_reviewer_objection: Simulated objection: I can identify the baseline families but cannot reproduce their particular adaptation and selection configurations or determine how matched the training signal was.

fix.instruction: Add a compact appendix baseline-protocol table reporting the actual Skill-Pro and SkillDAG feedback/objective, mutable state, training/validation data use, optimization budget or stopping rule, checkpoint choice, backbone and deliberate upstream deviations. Mark non-applicable fields explicitly for fixed graph construction or methods not trained in this study. Frame frozen SkillRouter as an off-the-shelf comparator, as the paper already does, and restrict superiority claims to the tested configurations. A new fine-tuned SkillRouter run is not required to fix this reporting issue.
required_inputs: Actual Skill-Pro and SkillDAG configuration/command records; do not infer missing settings from method names.
acceptance_criteria: Actual non-parametric baseline setup is reproducible from the paper/configuration reference.
Training signal, selection protocol and resource differences are stated, with non-applicable fields labeled.
No claim of controlled optimizer superiority beyond the tested setup; frozen SkillRouter remains explicitly frozen.

location.quoted_text: SkillRouter is the strongest routing baseline, yet RouterBSI the nDCG@1 and nDCG@10 is 10.9\% and 8.4\% higher on average.

issues.problem: The main comparative advantage is supported by point estimates without paired uncertainty for the reported method comparisons.
reasoning_chain: 1. Observed: Table 1 and Figure 4 report main competitor means; Appendix E.1 explicitly states one evaluation per method–retriever setting and no significance tests.

2. Internal scientific standard: task-matched comparisons should distinguish the observed effect from sampling and optimization variability; three retrieval conditions are not independent seed repetitions.
3. Counterevidence: the appendix transparently discloses the limitation, and Table 1 aggregates reproduce; the issue is inferential strength, not proven arithmetic error.
4. Consequence: the small downstream margins and per-dataset reversals have unknown comparative precision; the separate three-run component ablation does not quantify those gaps.
issues.predicted_reviewer_objection: Simulated objection: The main comparative advantage is supported by point estimates without paired uncertainty for the reported method comparisons.

fix.instruction: Where saved task-level outcomes exist, compute paired task-bootstrap intervals for RouterBSI minus SkillRouter routing and downstream metrics, preserving retriever pairing and dataset weights. Report that these intervals condition on the observed fitted policies. State single-run scope in main text. If predictions are unavailable, keep comparisons explicitly descriptive; do not fabricate intervals or require arbitrary additional seeds.
required_inputs: Saved paired task-level predictions for paired intervals, if available; no model rerun required for this analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Main comparisons report paired effect uncertainty or are explicitly limited to observed single-run descriptive estimates.
Task, retriever and seed variability are not conflated.
No statistical-significance claim without a stated test.

location.quoted_text: They also suggest that predicates reach a plateau that cannot be overcomed with more capable LLMs, where it's difficult for the predicate to be narrow enough to be false for irrelevant tasks but broad enough to be true for all relevant tasks

issues.problem: Three backbone endpoints do not establish an irreducible predicate-capacity ceiling.
reasoning_chain: 1. Observed: Figure 7 reports final nDCG@1 of 0.742, 0.802 and 0.745; the middle backbone has the strongest endpoint.
2. Internal scientific standard: a finite, single-run cross-model comparison cannot establish that greater capability cannot overcome a plateau or identify predicate expressivity as its cause.
3. Counterevidence: Section 7.3 correctly acknowledges nonmonotonic endpoints, and the 99.6% endpoint ratio is a valid descriptive comparison.
4. Consequence: the final mechanistic/scaling inference exceeds what those measurements distinguish from optimization, evaluator, task and model-family effects.
issues.predicted_reviewer_objection: Simulated objection: Three backbone endpoints do not establish an irreducible predicate-capacity ceiling.

fix.instruction: Replace only the unsupported ceiling sentence with a measured-scope statement; retain the actual endpoints. No new experiment is required if the claim is narrowed.
fix.target_text: These results show that final routing performance is not monotonic across the tested backbones; they do not establish an intrinsic ceiling on predicate-based routing.
acceptance_criteria: No claim of an irreducible ceiling from three endpoints.
Retain nonmonotonic final ordering and restrict generalization to tested models/settings.

location.quoted_text: This finding suggests expanding selected skills to include dependent skills could improve downstream performance even if the dependent skills are not required.

issues.problem: The dependency explanation is not isolated from differing skill budgets and baseline mechanisms.
reasoning_chain: 1. Observed: SkillDAG receives ten skills while RouterBSI top-k receives five; the main text explicitly discloses this.
2. Internal causal standard: different context budgets and selection mechanisms prevent attributing the downstream gap specifically to dependency utility.
3. Counterevidence: the sentence is already tentative (suggests/could), so this is a minor qualification rather than a demonstrated false empirical result.
4. Consequence: present dependency utility as a hypothesis, not a mechanism established by this comparison.

fix.instruction: Keep the future-work hypothesis but append the budget qualification. A matched-budget experiment is optional unless causal attribution is retained.

acceptance_criteria: The hypothesis explicitly acknowledges different supplied-skill budgets.
No claim that this comparison isolates dependency effects.

4. Consequence: readers can mistakenly interpret ablation F1 as a fixed-cutoff score or the 90.5% retention as unconditional end-to-end recall.

narrative_diagnostics.recoverable_thesis: Editable applicability predicates can improve skill routing without weight updates when proposed edits are selected with bounded replay and checked against held-out validation.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We propose RouterBSI, a non-parametric skill-routing framework that evaluates explicit applicability predicates over retrieved candidates, making routing criteria interpretable and directly editable without updating the underlying language model.
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: Interpretability is by explicit representation, not a measured human-usability result.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We develop a recursive self-improvement procedure that refines predicates from routing failures, selects updates through minimum Bayes risk over a bounded replay of relevant and irrelevant tasks, and rejects updates with higher held-out validation error than the cold-start predicate.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Risk/validation equations and Figure 5 component ablation
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: Keep cold-start-gate scope distinct from monotonic improvement over the previous policy.

contribution_ladder.claimed_contribution: We evaluate RouterBSI on six SRA-Bench datasets with a shared 26K-skill corpus, achieving the highest aggregate nDCG@10 and Hit@1 among evaluated methods while ablations establish the contributions of replay and validation.
contribution_ladder.asymmetry: Observed routing gains do not establish an intrinsic ceiling or uniformly best downstream utility.

narrative_issues: The core claim is routing improvement, not downstream supremacy; the conclusion mostly preserves this distinction.
Position the contribution as the predicate-routing/update combination; JTPRO and Skill-Pro are already cited, not missing references.
optional_editorial_notes: The interpretable-routing contribution would benefit from a main-text distinction between inspectable predicate text and imperfect semantic execution.
Limitations already acknowledges checker errors. An optional main diagnostic can distinguish textual inspectability from reliable execution; H.1 model agreement is not human-ground-truth accuracy.

The gate correctly compares to cold-start initialization. A compact note on iteration-start rollback and no-support behavior would be useful, but the already-correct equations do not warrant reopening the old replay contradiction.
